evidence.note: n+1: 'Avoid looping with separate queries'; use `include`, the `in` filter, or relationLoadStrategy 'join'.
Vendor study of 470 OSS PRs: AI-authored PRs had ~1.7x more issues; performance inefficiencies (excessive I/O, N+1 queries, unindexed lookups) ~8x more often; security issues 1.5-2x.

ts-perf-query-per-item.whyNotLinter: ESLint `no-await-in-loop` flags sequential awaits (any call), not per-item DB queries, and misses `Promise.all(items.map(query))`; no rule knows which calls hit the database.
ts-perf-query-per-item.aiRelevance: High (C): N+1 is named explicitly in the CodeRabbit AI-vs-human findings; `Promise.all(map(findUnique))` is a typical agent 'optimization'.

evidence.note: 'In a server, you should not use the following synchronous APIs': crypto/zlib/fs/child_process *Sync.

ts-perf-sync-io-in-handler.whyNotLinter: eslint-plugin-n `n/no-sync` (opt-in) bans every *Sync call literally and cannot tell startup/CLI code from per-request code, so most repos leave it off.
ts-perf-sync-io-in-handler.aiRelevance: Medium-high (inferred): agents write `fs.readFileSync` in route handlers because it is shorter.
ts-perf-sync-io-in-handler.expectedNoise: low -- the handler context must be visible.

evidence.note: Vulnerable when missing a limit on 'Number of records per page to return in a single request-response'; validate the parameter server-side.
Prisma performance guidance (pagination with take/skip/cursor is the documented pattern).

ts-perf-unbounded-list-query.whyNotLinter: No linter knows which tables grow or whether code is a request handler.
ts-perf-unbounded-list-query.aiRelevance: High (inferred): list endpoints generated by agents almost always start as `findMany()` with no `take`.
ts-perf-unbounded-list-query.expectedNoise: med -- small admin tables and user-scoped lists may be fine; the `false` list covers visible cases.

ts-perf-linear-lookup-in-loop.evidenceBar: BELOW BAR (only C). Needs an A-grade source (findings log or a repo guideline) or a second B before it ships as a built-in.
ts-perf-linear-lookup-in-loop.whyNotLinter: No ESLint/Biome rule detects nested collection scans; `unicorn` only suggests `includes` over `indexOf`.
ts-perf-linear-lookup-in-loop.aiRelevance: High (C): 'unindexed lookups' are listed among the AI performance findings.
ts-perf-linear-lookup-in-loop.expectedNoise: med -- sizes are rarely visible; small lists make it harmless but not wrong.
